epics.name: Help center (/help) and help content
epics.goal: A searchable help center shipped with the product (Markdown in the repo, one guide per ATS, billing stated plainly) that every surface links to instead of a mailto.

epics.name: Support conversations (tickets) with a visible reply
epics.goal: Every bug, question, billing or scam report becomes a ticket the user can see, the team answers in-product, and an SLA is measured.

epics.name: Job-scam safety centre
epics.goal: Learn, check and get warned: a public safety hub, a local rule-based 'Is this legit?' checker, warnings inside the application page, risk flags on postings, one-tap reporting and a blocklist.

epics.name: Extension in-page help and site reports
epics.goal: The drawer can say 'help me' and 'this site didn't fill' with consented diagnostics, and shows the fix when it ships.

epics.name: Feedback loops, feature requests, what's new
epics.goal: One feedback event for every thumbs, a public voted request board, a changelog that closes the loop, tiny CSAT/NPS and the store-review prompt.

epics.name: AI help assistant (grounded in help content)
epics.goal: Retrieval-first help answers with no model call on Free, Pro answers on a platform support budget, one-tap escalation with the transcript.

epics.name: Status page and incident communication
epics.goal: A public /status with per-ATS autofill state, human-written incidents, scoped banners in the app and the drawer, and subscriptions.

epics.name: Community
epics.goal: A small moderated Discord with an 'is this legit?' bot and product bridges; explicitly not a support channel; kill criteria defined.

epics.name: Support operations and knowledge
epics.goal: Metrics, tags, SUPPORT-role scoping, knowledge-gap reports and runbooks so a small team answers fast and the help center grows from real questions.

epics.name: Support policies, accessibility and localisation readiness
epics.goal: Published support policy and SLA, accessible support surfaces, help content ready for a second language, org-aware routing.

stories.title: @kiwiply/scam-rules: signal catalogue, scorer, scrubber and a 60-fixture corpus (shared by web, extension, API port)
stories.story: As the product I want one deterministic rules module that scores a message or posting for scam signals so that every surface warns the same way with no AI.
stories.genz: Protection that is identical on Free — safety is not a paid feature.
ac: packages/scam-rules (plain ES module, zero deps) exporting score(text, {url?, knownDomains?}) → {band, score, signals:[{id, weight, evidence, explain, types[]}], types[]}; signals.json is the single catalogue (ids/weights/regex/explanations) per design §2
Bands: 0–2 Looks normal · 3–5 Be careful · ≥ 6 Likely a scam; ATS/vendor domain allowlist suppresses domain_mismatch
scrub(text) removes emails, phones, card/SSN-like patterns; used before any storage
Fixture corpus: 30 scam + 30 legitimate samples (rewritten from public FTC/IC3/university examples); precision ≥ 0.9 on Likely, recall ≥ 0.8
Copied into the extension build like parser-core (engine stays dep-free)
tests: packages/scam-rules/test: corpus thresholds, per-signal unit tests, scrubber, allowlist
stories.tech: packages/scam-rules/{index.js,signals.json,allowlist.json,scrub.js}; job-autofill/scripts copy step mirrors web/scripts/sync-parser-core.mjs
stories.benchmark: G15. LinkedIn Safety Pulse 2026 red flags (sensitive-info requests 59%, upfront fees 56%, off-platform 38%); Handshake/UW/USC lists.

stories.title: /safety hub: nine scam-type pages and the 'Is this legit?' checker (client-side)

stories.genz: Gen Z: 32% victims vs Gen X 17%, and 32% ignore warning signs (LinkedIn 2026) — the checker is the friend who reads the message with you.
ac: /safety (marketing layout, public, no sign-in): checker first (textarea + URL, 'checked on your device — nothing is sent'), nine type pages /safety/<type> from web/content/safety/*.md, the 'It happened — what now' entry (S3.8), live aggregate count placeholder

Result view: band, each triggered signal with evidence snippet + plain explanation, matched types, next steps, [Report this] (S3.3), [Not a scam? Tell us] feedback, Pro-only [Explain for me] placeholder (S6.2)
Nothing pasted leaves the device unless Report is tapped; no analytics on the text
Linked from /help privacy-safety, the footer and the job cards (S3.5)

stories.title: Extension 'Heads up' banner before the first fill (SSN/bank before offer, payment, domain mismatch)

ac: Permission map (A0.3) gains SUPPORT_TICKETS_READ/WRITE, HELP_STATS_READ, SAFETY_REVIEW; SUPPORT role has these and nothing from billing/AI budgets/PII exports
Reading a ticket whose reporter is anonymous (email only) writes a USER_PII_VIEW LOW audit row; 'view as' remains A1.5
Ticket DTOs for SUPPORT omit email domain-level info beyond what is needed to reply
tests: SupportRoleIT (403 on billing endpoints; ticket read allowed; audit row)
stories.tech: api security/Permissions (A0.3), AdminSupportTicketResource @PreAuthorize, AdminAuditService

stories.title: Support runbooks as admin-only playbooks (refund script, account recovery, extension debugging, scam triage, engineering escalation)
stories.story: As a new support teammate I want the five scripts we actually use so that replies are consistent and honest from day one.
stories.genz: The 'no refunds, cancel anytime' reply is kind, clear and the same every time.
ac: web/content/support-playbooks/*.md rendered at /admin/playbooks (ADMIN/SUPPORT only, same renderer as /help): refunds (none — script + what we can do: fix, extend on our error via A2.4 comps), account recovery (resend verification, change email A1.4), extension debugging checklist (version, adapter, site report), scam triage (outcomes, blocklist), engineering escalation (ticket → GitHub issue link convention)
Macros (S2.6) seeded from the playbooks
tests: build validation; admin route 403 for users
stories.tech: web/src/app/(admin)/admin/playbooks/[slug]/page.tsx; content under web/content/support-playbooks/

stories.title: Published support policy: channels, hours, SLA by plan, what we never do, languages — on /help and the contact page
stories.story: As a user I want to know how support works and how fast before I pay so that there are no surprises.
stories.genz: State it plainly; competitors' one-star reviews are about surprises.
ac: /help/a/how-support-works: in-app tickets (primary), email fallback, hours, first-response targets from settings `support.sla_business_days.*` (defaults Pro/Autopilot 1, Free 2, site/scam reports 1), languages (English; Spanish pilot when S10.3 lands), what we never do (ask for passwords, auto-submit, move money, read your resume files without consent), 'no refunds, cancel anytime' link

Contact page and ticket sheet read the same copy from one source — the evaluated config (`support.sla_business_days.*` via GET /api/config/public, A5.9) rendered by web/src/lib/support-policy.ts, never a constants file — so numbers never drift; the policy numbers are the ones S9.1 measures
tests: unit: policy constants used by sheet and page
stories.tech: web/content/help/getting-started/how-support-works.md generated/validated against web/src/lib/support-policy.ts
stories.benchmark: Jobscan/Simplify complaints about silence and refund surprises; Huntr's written (hedged) policy.

stories.title: Accessibility of every support surface (sheets, checker, thread, status) with axe in CI
stories.story: As a screen-reader or keyboard user I want help, reporting and safety tools to work fully so that support is not the least accessible part of the product.
stories.genz: Accessibility is a baseline expectation, not a setting.
ac: Focus trap + Escape on every sheet; 44 px targets; aria-live for ticket status/CSAT thanks; reduced-motion respected; checker result readable in order; status page colour + text (never colour alone)
axe (U19.1 harness) runs on /help, /help/a/[slug], /safety, /status, the ticket thread and the Help sheet with zero serious violations
tests: axe CI job over the listed routes
stories.tech: web Playwright + @axe-core/playwright (U19.3 infra); packages/ui Sheet/ThumbsFeedback a11y props

stories.title: Help and safety content i18n readiness (locale folders, fallback, hreflang) with a Spanish pilot of the top 10 + safety hub
stories.story: As a Spanish-speaking job seeker in the US I want the safety hub and the top help articles in Spanish so that the most vulnerable audience isn't left out.
stories.genz: Scam targeting is heaviest on new-to-market and immigrant job seekers (FTC).
ac: web/content/help/<locale>/ and safety/<locale>/ with fallback to en; /help/es/... routes; hreflang tags; build validates every es file has an en twin
Pilot: the 10 most-viewed articles (from S1.4 stats) + the nine safety pages + what-now in Spanish (human-reviewed; machine draft allowed)
UI chrome strings for help/safety/status extracted (U19 string extraction convention)
stories.tech: web/scripts/build-help-index.mjs locale support; web/src/app/(marketing)/help/[locale]? routing per U19.4 convention

stories.title: Org-aware support routing: member tickets carry org id (consent-scoped), org admin contact path with priority, STAFF sees counts only
stories.story: As an org admin I want a priority support path for my organisation while my members' tickets stay private so that support respects the consent model.
stories.genz: Your school can't read your support thread.
ac: support_ticket.org_id NULL additive, set from the member's active org at create; org admin 'Contact support' creates a kind=QUESTION ticket with priority 1 and tag org:<id>
Org dashboard shows only counts of open member tickets (never subjects/bodies); STAFF role (O5.4) sees counts for their members only; platform support sees all
Metrics (S9.1) split by org for the owner
tests: OrgSupportScopeIT (org admin cannot read member ticket 404; counts only; priority set)
stories.tech: api SupportTicketService org hook (O1.1 tenant model), AdminSupportTicketResource org filter; web (org) settings contact sheet
